message.content:
### Killing Visual Studio Code (`code.exe`) from the Windows command line

> **TL;DR**  
> ```cmd
> taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
> ```

Below is a quick‑start guide, plus a few handy variations and troubleshooting tips.

---

## 1. Open a Command Prompt (or PowerShell)

```cmd
cmd
```

or

```powershell
powershell
```

---

## 2. Find the process (optional)

If you want to see which VS Code instances are running and their PIDs:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

Output will look like:

```
Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
========================= ======== ================ =========== ============
code.exe                   12345 Console                    1     150,000 K
code.exe                   67890 Console                    1     152,000 K
```

---

## 3. Kill all VS Code processes

### Basic force‑kill

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

- `/IM code.exe` – target the image name.
- `/F` – force termination (no graceful shutdown).

### Force‑kill **and** all child processes

VS Code spawns helper processes (`code.exe` children). To kill them all:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

- `/T` – terminate the specified process and any child processes started by it.

---

## 4. Kill a specific instance by PID

If you only want to kill one instance (e.g., the one with PID 12345):

```cmd
taskkill /PID 12345 /F
```

---

## 5. Kill only your user’s VS Code processes

If multiple users are logged in and you want to avoid killing others’ VS Code:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "USERNAME eq %USERNAME%"
```

---

## 6. Using PowerShell (alternative)

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or with PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id 12345 -Force
```

---

## 7. Common pitfalls & fixes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| `taskkill` reports “The process cannot be terminated” | Process is protected or already exiting | Use `/F` (force) or wait a few seconds and try again |
| `taskkill` cannot find `code.exe` | VS Code not in PATH or running under a different name | Use full path: `taskkill /IM "C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe" /F` |
| VS Code restarts immediately | Another instance is launching it (e.g., via a shortcut or startup script) | Disable the auto‑launch mechanism or kill the launcher first |

---

## 8. Quick cheat sheet

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Force‑kill all VS Code processes |
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` | Force‑kill all VS Code processes **and** their children |
| `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Force‑kill a specific instance |
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "USERNAME eq <user>"` | Kill only your user’s VS Code |
| `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent |

---

### Bottom line

The simplest, most reliable way to shut down VS Code from the command line is:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

That will terminate the main `code.exe` process and any helper processes it spawned, ensuring VS Code is fully closed.
